review_notes: I read the whole file. I grepped Mathlib for other uses of the archimedean-class concept (HahnEmbedding, Lex, DivisibleHull, Hyperreal, StandardPart, Ring/Archimedean, Module/Archimedean). Those files build on this file's `ArchimedeanClass`, so they are not competing definitions. Reusing existing Mathlib infrastructure here looks sound: `Antisymmetrization`, `Quotient.lift`, `WithTop.subtypeOrderIso` and `UpperSet`. The type synonyms `MulArchimedeanOrder` and `MulArchimedeanClass` are deliberate and documented. The two `subgroup` families are `MulArchimedeanClass.subgroup`, which uses a junk value at `⊤`, and `FiniteMulArchimedeanClass.subgroup`, which is defined on finite classes. They are an intentional pair that share carriers and are linked by `toUpperSetMulArchimedeanClass`. The `withTopOrderIso` and `congrOrderIso` declarations are thin named specialisations. I found no independent existing Mathlib concept that this file re-implements, so I am abstaining. I did not search every Mathlib directory exhaustively for an unrelated equivalent of `lift`, `lift₂` or `liftOrderHom`.
